title: Records (-record): Compile-Time Tuple Sugar, #rec.field Indices & Header Files
solutionExplanation: Declares -record(frame, {...}) and demonstrates record instantiation, update, #frame.seq tuple offset extraction, and lists:keyfind integration.

otpDocCards.description: Tagged tuple wrapper providing named field access with O(1) tuple speed.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Exact same speed and memory footprint as raw tagged tuples.

mentalModelCheck.question: What does the expression #frame.seq evaluate to at compile time for -record(frame, {seq = 0, type = data, payload}).?

options.label: The integer 2, representing the 1-indexed tuple position of seq within the underlying {frame, Seq, Type, Payload} tuple
options.explanation: In Erlang tuples, element 1 is the record tag frame, so seq is at index 2.

options.label: The default value 0 defined in the record specification
options.explanation: Default values are only used when instantiating new records without explicit values; #record.field is an index offset.

options.label: The atom seq
options.explanation: #record.field evaluates to an integer index, not an atom.
